newsitem.title: GERMANY: Kohl allies cleared of fraud in east Germany.
newsitem.headline: Kohl allies cleared of fraud in east Germany.

text.p: Two west German former allies of Chancellor Helmut Kohl, brought to east Germany after unification to become ministers in a regional state cabinet, were acquitted of fraud charges on Thursday.

Werner Muench, one-time premier of Saxony-Anhalt state, and his former social affairs minister Werner Schreiber were accused of giving false information about their previous salaries as members of parliament to boost their pay illegally.
But prosecutors conceded on Wednesday that they had not proved that the two members of Kohl's Christian Democrats had deliberately falsified statements of their previous incomes.
Muench had previously been a member of the European parliament, Schreiber a member of the federal parliament in Bonn.
On Thursday, the judge acquitted the men.
Salaries of politicians in east Germany were by law lower than those of their western colleagues at the time.
But western politicians who showed they had earned more in their previous post were not expected to take a drop in pay, and were entitled to go on receiving this amount.

Saxony-Anhalt's entire state cabinet quit in 1993 after the regional audit office accused Schreiber, Muench and two other ministers brought in from the west of fraud to the tune of 900,000 marks ($600,000) by overstating their previous pay.
Charges against two of the men were subsequently dropped.
